note: The Stage 0 constants of Fast QC v10: PCM16StreamLimiter, StreamingExecutionContext.AudioQCThresholds and AudioSpeakingRateQC. Swift owns them; AudioQCStage0CalibrationTests asserts the Swift values equal this record, and scripts/tests/test_audio_qc.py asserts the Python mirror's FASTQC does. They are legacy-unqualified bounds (A10), not qualified operating points: a qualified change writes a new record for a new algorithm version and edits Swift, the mirror and the record together.

speakingRateFastCalibration.rule: A take whose duration over its conservative units (AudioSpeakingRateQC.conservativeUnits: letters and digits, a run of decimal digits once, a run of one repeated letter at most twice, no lone Hangul compatibility letter) falls below fastSecondsPerUnit, with at least minimumJudgedUnits such units, fails speaking_rate_fast (instability). Each bound is half the fastest human clip of its class on the same count; a class with no human clip has none (null) and is not judged.
speakingRateFastCalibration.replay: The quality screens' 1,496 distinct judged takes (1,131 alphabetic, 168 Chinese, 197 Korean): it fails one, a full German sentence in 0.32 s (0.0082 s per unit, both recognizers wrong), and no other; the fastest accepted take runs at 0.0412 s per unit with both recognizers exact. The 367 committed benchmark rows that carry a rate run at 0.060 s per unit or slower.

silenceSource.rule: Silent runs (dropout, cadence and terminal silence) are judged on the take as written, before the publication watermark; level, DC, clipping and format stay judged on the published, marked bytes.
silenceSource.why: The watermark lifts samples a take wrote below the 0.001 floor above it on every take of the clone screen (191 of 191, deltas up to 1,731 LSB at speech edges), cutting silent runs apart: one take's 611 ms of trailing silence read as 38 ms on the marked file, another's 313 ms as 5 ms; 125 of 191 longest interior runs read shorter. Since marking shipped (2026-08-07) Fast QC undercounted dropouts and terminal silence; the mirror, which never marks, already measured silence this way.
